title: Finite tensor savings and exact Fourier circuits
summary: We construct exact nonuniform Fourier circuits of size $`o(n\log n)`$ along an unbounded sequence of lengths, counting every addition, subtraction, and scalar multiplication. This refutes the $`\Omega(n\log n)`$ lower bound in the unrestricted complex linear-circuit model. The construction uses a finite tensor saving: a tensor power of some invertible nonmonomial complex matrix can be computed with fewer matrix calls than the standard tensor-axis algorithm on the same coordinates, when invertible monomial maps are allowed freely between calls.

review.reason: Constructs exact Fourier circuits with fewer operations, using a finite tensor saving in linear-circuit complexity.
